instrument_name: Indiana Minimum Wage Law of 1965, IC 22-2-2-3 and 22-2-2-4 (IC 2026, Title 22 Art. 2)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer = 2+ employees in a workweek and NOT subject to FLSA minimum wage. 22-2-2-4(c): minimum wage = the FLSA minimum wage (no own figure; 7.25 USD/h federal). (d) tip credit: cash wage not less than 2.13 USD/h, employer supports tip credit by reported tips. (f) overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/workweek; no daily overtime; (n) domestic service also 40 h rule. Exempt from the state law: persons under 16; agricultural labour; student nurses/students working for own school; religious-order members and ministers; commission-only employees; executives earning 150+/week; persons employed no more than 4 weeks in any 4 consecutive 3-month periods; motor carrier; direct sellers; minor-league baseball (22-2-2-3(a)-(r)).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-2-10.5 Prohibition against unit establishing a higher minimum wage; IC 22-2-16-3 prohibition on local benefit/leave mandates
figure_or_rule_carried: No local minimum wage: a unit (county, city, town, IC 36-1-2-23) may not establish/mandate a minimum wage above IC 22-2-2-4 or the federal 29 USC 206(a)(1) (P.L.211-2011, amended P.L.144-2016). A unit may not mandate any benefit, term of employment, working condition or attendance/scheduling/leave policy exceeding federal/state law (IC 22-2-16-3, P.L.88-2013, amended P.L.120-2016): no local paid sick leave ordinances; does not apply to a unit's own employees or to unit contracts/incentive terms (22-2-16-1).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-5 Payment of wages (frequency, timing, method; voluntary separation)
figure_or_rule_carried: Pay at least semimonthly, or biweekly if requested; in US money, negotiable check, draft, money order, or electronic transfer to the financial institution designated by the employee (no paycard named). Wages earned to a date not more than 10 business days before payday. Voluntary leaver: paid at the next usual and regular payday; if whereabouts unknown, penalty not triggered until 10 business days after demand or address furnished. FLSA-overtime-eligible salaried employees exempt from s.1 (1.1). Failure: unpaid wages + attorney fee; if not in good faith, liquidated damages 2x the wages due (22-2-5-2, P.L.193-2015). Farmers/agriculture exempt from the chapter (22-2-5-3).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-6 Wage deductions (wage assignments, overpayment recovery), two 2026 versions (P.L.104-2026 s.22 and P.L.115-2026 s.14)
figure_or_rule_carried: Any employee-directed deduction = wage assignment, valid only if written, signed by employee, revocable on written notice, agreed in writing by employer, copy delivered to employer within 10 days, and for a listed purpose (insurance, charity, US bonds, employer stock, union dues, employer merchandise, employer loan, health/pension plans, credit union, uniforms/tools at direct cost, training reimbursement, payroll/vacation advance, etc.). Interest on employer loans/advances <= Fed prime + 4%. Uniform/tool assignments capped at lesser of 2,500 USD/year or 5% of weekly disposable earnings; no charge for OSHA PPE. Overpayment recovery: 2 weeks notice; cap lesser of 25% of weekly disposable earnings or excess over 30x federal minimum hourly wage; decimal-point error of 10x gross may be recovered at once (22-2-6-4). Two versions in IC 2026: P.L.104-2026 adds (b)(19) political-subdivision deferred retirement (opt-out, no (a) formalities); P.L.115-2026 re-points UCCC refs IC 24-4.5 -> IC 37-2/37-3 (consumer-credit recodification). Effective dates of the two acts not shown in the compilation.

instrument_name: IC 22-2-9-2 Wages due on separation by the employer (Wage Claims Act)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer separates the employee from the payroll: unpaid wages due at the regular payday for the pay period in which separation occurred (railroads excepted). Industrial-dispute suspension: due at the next regular payday. 'Wages' = all amounts recompensing labour, any method of calculation. Disputed amounts: employer pays the amount it concedes (22-2-9-3). Voluntary resignation governed by IC 22-2-5-1(b) (next usual payday).

instrument_name: IC 22-2-13 Military family leave
figure_or_rule_carried: Unpaid military family leave up to 10 working days per calendar year for spouse/parent/grandparent/child/sibling of a person ordered to active duty (12 months service, 1,500 hours); employee may elect or employer may require substitution of paid vacation/personal leave (not sick leave); health benefits continue. No Indiana statute mandates paid sick leave for private employers (none located in IC 22-2) and local mandates are pre-empted (IC 22-2-16-3).

instrument_name: Indiana DOR Departmental Notice #1, Effective Oct. 1, 2026 (R47 / 10-26): How to Compute Withholding for State and County Income Tax
article_or_section: pp.1-5 (deduction constant Tables A/B/C, example, nonresident 30-day rule, county rate chart)
figure_or_rule_carried: State AGI rate 2026 2.95%. Method: taxable = gross per period - deduction constants (WH-4 line 5 personal exemptions 1,000/yr each incl. 65+/blind; lines 6 and 7 dependent and first-time dependent 1,500/yr each; line 8 adopted child 3,000/yr; constants = annual amount / pay periods: weekly 52, biweekly 26, semimonthly 24, monthly 12, daily 365) x 2.95% state, x county rate county tax. Bonus/one-time payments withheld without exemptions. Indiana does not follow IRC 3402(n) no-withholding allowance. Official worked example: weekly 800, 5 personal + 3 dep + 1 first-time + 2 adopted, county 0.01: constants 326.92, taxable 473.08, state 13.96, county 4.73 (re-derived 2026-11-02). County of residence on Jan 1, or if out-of-state resident on Jan 1, county of principal work on Jan 1. Nonresident 30-day rule (from 2024-01-01): no state/county withholding if employee expected to work in Indiana 30 days or less (time-and-attendance system or Form WH-4AFF), catch-up if exceeded; not for athletes/entertainers/public figures or part-year residents. County rate changes since Jan 1, 2026 edition (asterisked): Boone 0.0171 (was 0.017). Full 92-county chart on p.5 (e.g. Marion 0.0202, Porter 0.005, Randolph 0.03).

instrument_name: Indiana DOR Income Tax Information Bulletin #32, General Information on Local Income Taxes (Dec 2024)
figure_or_rule_carried: Local Income Tax (LIT) replaced CAGIT/COIT/CEDIT from tax year 2017; all 92 counties have a LIT. County of residence and county of principal business/employment fixed as of Jan 1 for the whole year; a mid-year move requires a new WH-4 but only sets the county for the next year. Residents: county rate on whole Indiana AGI; nonresidents with principal work in an Indiana county: same rate on income derived from that county; reciprocity does not apply to county tax; no separate nonresident LIT rate. Rate caps: expenditure rate up to 2.5% (2.75% Marion), +1.25% property tax relief, special purpose rates (IC 6-3.6-5/-6/-7). Rate-change timing: ordinance Jan 1-Aug 31 -> effective Oct 1 same year; Sep 1-Oct 31 -> Jan 1 next year; Nov 1-Dec 31 -> Oct 1 next year. 30-day nonresident safe harbor IC 6-3-2-27.5 from 2024 (employees only; not team members, entertainers, contractors). Credit against county tax for out-of-state local tax (residents only).

instrument_name: Indiana DOR Tax Rates, Fees & Penalties page (individual AGI rate 2026 and 2027)
figure_or_rule_carried: 'The Indiana Individual adjusted gross income tax rate for 2026 is 2.95% and will adjust in 2027 to 2.90%.' County rates may be adjusted in January and October; Departmental Notice #1 has the current chart. Statutory basis IC 6-3-2-1 (not read on an official host: iga.in.gov is a script-rendered SPA). 2.95% matches DN#1 R47 (US-INS5-007): second document family on the same authority.

instrument_name: Indiana DOR Withholding Income page: WH-1 / WH-3, electronic filing, file formats
article_or_section: Forms WH-1 and WH-3; Electronic Filing of Withholding Taxes; Choosing your file format
figure_or_rule_carried: WH-1 = periodic return (report and remit), monthly, early-monthly or annual, via INTIME or SFTP; WH-3 = annual reconciliation matching WH-1 totals to wage statements, due January 31, INTIME or SFTP. Late penalty WH-1 up to 20% (min 5 USD); WH-3 10 USD per wage statement. Zero returns still required once registered. More than 25 W-2/W-2G/1099-R statements -> electronic filing mandatory (IC 6-3-4-16.5). INTIME upload under 10 MB; SFTP above 10 MB. Formats: DOR Withholding XML schema IDORWTH2016V1.0 with WH-1 and WH-3 XML business rules; IRS IRIS XML; 1220 flat file (DOR retiring September 2027); EFW2 flat file with Indiana deviations. Registration via INBiz; EIN required.

instrument_name: Indiana DOR EFW2 (W-2 and WH-3) Electronic Filing Requirements, 2025 and Prior Tax Years (last revised Oct 2025)
article_or_section: Important Reminders; Administrative Highlights; Code RS State Record; Appendix A county codes
figure_or_rule_carried: Indiana accepts SSA EFW2 for W-2/WH-3; only the RS record is Indiana-specific: pos. 306-307 county code (Appendix A, 2 digits), 309-319 local taxable wages (11), 320-330 local income tax withheld (11), 331-340 Indiana TID (10), 341-343 TID location (3) - 13 digits mandatory or file rejected. One RS record for county tax (county of residence/work on Jan 1); two RS records allowed when amounts overflow. Filing deadline January 31 (next business day if weekend/holiday). Guide applies only to current EFW2 filers: new filers must use XML through INTIME or SFTP. Edition labelled '2025 and prior tax years': the TY2026 edition was not located.

instrument_name: Indiana DOR Business Tax FAQ: withholding filing frequency, EFT, records, W-2
figure_or_rule_carried: WH-1 filing status by monthly average tax withheld: 83.33 USD or less = annual, due 30 days after end of the period; 1,000 USD or less = monthly, due 30 days after month end; more than 1,000 USD = early filer, due 20 days after month end. Average monthly tax over 5,000 USD -> payments by EFT. Status reviewed each November for the next year; can increase, not decrease, frequency. All withholding filed and paid electronically (INTIME). If employer must withhold federal income tax it must withhold Indiana state and county tax. Casual laborers, some domestic employees, ministers and pension recipients may choose no withholding. Records: employee list by period, pay period, salaries, SSNs, county of residence on Jan 1, county of work. W-2 to employee by January 31; FAQ says copy to DOR by February 28 - CONFLICTS with the withholding page and EFW2 guide (January 31, US-INS5-010/011): use January 31.

instrument_name: Indiana DWD Unemployment Insurance Employer Handbook (revised 07/01/2025)
article_or_section: UI at a Glance p.7; Getting Started pp.11-14; New Hire Reporting p.22-23; New Employer Premium Rate p.23; Quarterly Employer Reporting pp.26-30; E S S / UPLINK reporting p.39-40
figure_or_rule_carried: '2011 to 2025: premiums are based on the first 9,500 of wages per employee per calendar year': minimum 0.50% (47.50), typical new employer 2.50% (237.50), maximum in good standing 7.40% (703.00), maximum delinquent 9.40% (902.50) [9,500 x rate re-derived]. Employer-only premiums (no employee contribution). New employer 2.5% for first four calendar years (rates set as of June 30 for next year); construction NAICS 23 = lesser of 4.0% or construction average (2.50% for 2025); government 1.6%; successors inherit 0.50%-9.4%. Coverage: domestic household help 1,000 USD cash wages in any calendar quarter; agricultural 20,000 USD cash wages in a calendar quarter (or 10 workers/20 weeks per handbook); clergy excluded. Quarterly wage and employment report (all wages for the year once liable; NTR quarters) due Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31; electronic filing mandatory since 2019 unless waiver (646 IAC 5-2-2); electronic payment required (646 IAC 5-2-17); E S S/UPLINK manual entry up to 50 workers, file (CSV or Indiana-modified ICESA) required above 50; SOC code (first 6 digits) and start date per worker; 25 USD fine per missing/inadequate report (invalid SSN/ITIN = inadequate). New hire: IC 22-4.1-4-2 and PRWORA, all employers report new hires and rehires after a 60-day break within 20 days of hire (first day of work), electronically to the Indiana New Hire Reporting Center (in-newhire.com); fine 25 USD per employee, up to 500 USD if conspiracy. UI poster required. Max weekly benefit 390, min 37.

instrument_name: Indiana DWD State Premium Rate Computation page (Wayback snapshot 2026-01-13, still carrying the 2025 rate year)
article_or_section: New 2025 Employer Premium Rates; rate types; applied rate schedules
figure_or_rule_carried: Applied rate = premium rate + solvency surcharge; solvency surcharge for 2025 = 0% of premium; applied premium rate = premium rate x 1.00 (interest surcharge). Types: new employer 2.5% regular / 2.50% NAICS 23 / 1.6% government; penalty rate = computed rate + 2% (failure to file reports or pay within 10 days of Merit Rate Delinquency Notice); merit rate from experience balance at June 30 vs past 36 months' payroll, schedule by credit or debit reserve. 2026 rate-year content (surcharge, schedule) NOT on this snapshot: open.

instrument_name: Indiana New Hire Reporting Center: Home (SB 148 changes) and Reporting Fundamentals
authority: Indiana New Hire Reporting Center (State of Indiana; operated by contractor Stellarware)
article_or_section: Home 'Changes to reporting requirements'; Reporting Fundamentals (who, what, when)
figure_or_rule_carried: From 2024-07-01 (Indiana Senate Bill 148) new hire and rehire reports must be filed electronically and must carry 4 new elements: current job title, primary SOC code, starting compensation, rate of pay basis (annual/hourly/other). Report all employees who reside or work in Indiana, rehires returning after 60+ days of layoff/furlough/separation/unpaid leave; temp agencies report once per hire. Required employer fields: FEIN (same as quarterly wage report), name, payroll address. Required employee fields: name (first, middle, last), mailing address, SSN, date of hire, job title, SOC, starting salary, rate of pay; optional: state of hire, date of birth, employer contact data. Deadline: within 20 days of hire/rehire (42 USC 653a); file submitters send two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart. Channels: web entry, web upload/SFTP (layouts on File Transfer page). Statute IC 22-4.1-4-2 (per DWD handbook, US-INS5-014). Fine 25 USD per unreported employee (handbook).

instrument_name: Indiana DCS Child Support Bureau: Indiana's Income Withholding Law, employer FAQ
authority: Indiana Department of Child Services, Child Support Bureau
figure_or_rule_carried: Applies to all employers regardless of size; IWO for child support only. Withholding begins no later than the first pay period occurring within 14 days after the IWO was mailed/faxed/served; remit to INSCCU each time the employee is paid. Employer with 50+ employees and more than one employee with an order must remit electronically. CCPA limits 50% / 55% (other dependents, under/over 12 weeks arrears) and 60% / 65% (no other dependents). Disposable earnings = after legally required deductions (taxes, social security); voluntary deductions and union dues stay in. Priority: child support over any other claim except current federal, state and local taxes; business garnishments limited to the remaining room under the 25% Indiana/CCPA limit. Lump sums (severance, accumulated sick/vacation pay, commissions, bonus) subject to arrears withholding up to the CCPA limit (contact EMU). Multiple IWOs prorated (DCS Prorate Calculator). Employer fee: optional 2.00 USD per withholding forwarded to INSCCU (inside the CCPA limit: if limit reached, remit limit minus 2.00). Annual Support Fee (ASFE) IWO counts within CCPA limit. Employer liable for amounts not withheld; up to 5,000 USD civil recovery for retaliation. NMSN for health coverage. Independent-contractor payments also subject to IWO.

instrument_name: Indiana Attorney General: Security Breaches page (Disclosure of Security Breach law)
authority: Indiana Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Indiana's Disclosure of Security Breach law requires Indiana businesses to inform affected persons of security breaches exposing personal information; the AG can seek up to 150,000 USD for breaches not properly disclosed; business FAQ and notification form on the AG site. Statute (IC 24-4.9) not read on an official host. No Indiana rule on SSN truncation on pay statements was located (IC 22-2-2-8 lists content only; not a negative proof).

instrument_name: Indiana Form WH-4, State Form 48845, Employee's Withholding Exemption and County Status Certificate (R10 / 8-23)
figure_or_rule_carried: Edition R10/8-23 (current download as of Wayback 2026-10-11). Kept by employer, not sent to DOR. Fields: name, SSN or ITIN, home address, Indiana county of residence on Jan 1, Indiana county of principal employment on Jan 1, box for county change effective next calendar year; line 1 self (1), line 2 spouse (1), line 3 dependents, line 4 65+/blind boxes, line 5 total (lines 1-4 = personal exemptions for DN#1 Table A), line 6 additional dependent exemption (child under 19, or under 24 full-time student), line 7 first-time additional dependent (valid only for the calendar year submitted; new WH-4 every year), line 8 adopted dependent, line 9 additional state withholding per period, line 10 additional county withholding per period (not binding on employer). Nonresident alien: only one exemption, line 1 = 1, skip to line 9. Employee who neither lived nor worked in Indiana on Jan 1 enters 'not applicable'. New WH-4 within 10 days when exemptions decrease (divorce, loss of support, dependent no longer qualifies). Dependent gross income test 4,400 USD (form text).
